name: Neogen Corporation

profile.description: Neogen Corporation develops, manufactures, and markets products dedicated to food and animal safety worldwide. The Food Safety segment (about 73% of Q1 FY2027 revenue) offers diagnostic test kits and culture media for pathogen, allergen, mycotoxin, and environmental monitoring, anchored by the Petrifilm platform acquired with 3M's Food Safety business in 2022. The Animal Safety segment provides animal genomics, veterinary instruments, and biosecurity products. CEO Mike Nassif (appointed August 2025, formerly of Siemens Healthineers) is leading a turnaround focused on execution discipline, organic innovation, and margin expansion.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The 3M Food Safety merger nearly doubled revenue from $527M (FY2022) to $924M (FY2024), but integration stumbles led to a $1.09B FY2025 net loss and revenue slipping to $870.4M in FY2026; the turnaround is only now showing traction with Q1 FY2027 core growth of 8.1% [1][3]. AI Deployment (1/2): Management's 2026 Investor Day emphasized innovation as a growth lever, but no quantified AI-driven revenue or savings were disclosed in recent results [2]. Market Share (1/2): Petrifilm is a widely used indicator-testing standard and Food Safety grew 7.4% to $163.2M in Q1 FY2027, but Neogen is one of several players alongside bioMerieux and others rather than a clear share gainer [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Nassif said in April 2026 the company was building 'the foundation for true organic innovation for the first time,' with FY2031 financial targets set at the October 2026 Investor Day, though specific next-gen product launch dates were not quantified [2][6]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FY2026 R&D of $18.4M was just 2.1% of revenue, well below diagnostics peers [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Neogen frames its work around global food security and human and animal well-being, a specific purpose that connects pathogen and allergen testing to preventing foodborne illness, and its annual report ties products to reducing waste through food safety, integrated pest management, and genetic selection [5]. Community Impact (1/2): The products themselves protect public health and the company publishes sustainability disclosures, but no distinctive foundation or quantified community investment program was found [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): Nassif conducted a rapid refresh of the executive team after the 2025 CEO change, and no data pointing to above-average retention was found [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying in the last 12 months was found.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 6 of 7 growth metrics (Forward PEG unavailable: the provider's forward PEG is negative/not meaningful because GAAP earnings are negative). D/E of 37.1% beats the 70% target (1.0) and 5yr revenue CAGR of 13.2% (FY2021 $468.5M to FY2026 $870.4M, derived from reported income statements, inflated by the 3M merger) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [3][4]. Q1 FY2027 revenue growth of 6.5% scores 0.88 and forward P/E of 26.3 scores 0.84, but TTM ROE of -2.7% and profit margin of -6.3% both score 0, with GAAP net loss of $11.9M in Q1 even as adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 18.7% [1][4]. Weighted 4.73/8 = 5.9, rounded to 6. Liquidity floor cleared: 3.33M avg volume x $11.82 = $39.4M daily [4].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Neogen sells physical diagnostic consumables (culture media, Petrifilm plates, test kits) and genomics services used in regulated food-safety programs; food must be physically sampled and tested, so AI cannot substitute for the core product, and no analyst commentary flags AI displacement risk [1][2]. Some exposure exists in data/analytics layers of environmental monitoring, where software-native competitors could add AI-driven predictive tools faster than Neogen, keeping this just below the immune tier. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI-related revenue was disclosed in Q1 FY2027 results or the 2026 Investor Day materials found [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: Neogen has a genuine food-safety purpose, but through Sinek's lens the past four years read more like a company fighting for stability than one advancing a cause: an overpriced transformational merger, a $1.09B write-down, a CEO change, and a sweeping executive refresh. Nassif's emphasis on 'disciplined operational execution' and FY2031 targets is a healthy reset, yet the institutional culture that sustains an infinite mindset has to be rebuilt.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Advancing food security and human and animal well-being is distinctive and service-oriented, and the 3M Food Safety deal can be traced to expanding that mission globally [5]. It has not yet been validated through a successful crisis test - the merger's value destruction ($1.09B FY2025 loss) shows the cause did not prevent overreach [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The 2025 CEO transition was followed by what analysts described as a rapid refresh of the executive team, and management's language centers on 'instilling a culture of disciplined operational execution' - a necessary but control-oriented message [6]. No evidence of strong tenure, low turnover, or psychological safety was found.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management commentary focuses on market share recovery and execution rather than acknowledging competitors such as bioMerieux as benchmarks that reveal Neogen's weaknesses [2][6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The 3M Food Safety combination reshaped the company's scale and product mix, and Nassif is now redirecting toward organic innovation for the first time [2][3]. This was an additive bet rather than abandoning a core business, so it is meaningful but not transformative in Sinek's sense.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The board replaced the CEO mid-integration and new leadership set multi-year FY2031 targets and organic-innovation investment rather than chasing quarterly beats [2]. Offsetting this, R&D spending fell from $26.0M in FY2023 to $18.4M in FY2026, the opposite of investing through a downturn [3].

investment_thesis: Neogen's turnaround is gaining traction. Q1 FY2027 revenue rose 6.5% to $222.8M with core growth of 8.1%, Food Safety grew 7.4% to $163.2M, Animal Safety returned to growth (+4.2% to $59.6M), and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 18.7% from 17.0% [1]. Management raised FY2027 guidance to $885-890M revenue and $181-183M adjusted EBITDA, and the October 2026 Investor Day laid out a plan for growth, innovation, and margin expansion through FY2031 [1][2]. The balance sheet is conservative for a recovering business (D/E 37%, current ratio 3.9x), and the stock trades at 26x forward earnings and roughly 1.2x book value [4]. Food-safety testing is a recurring, regulation-driven consumables business with secular tailwinds from tightening global food standards.
thesis_continued: The bear case is that GAAP profitability remains elusive: Neogen posted a $11.9M net loss in Q1 FY2027, TTM profit margin is -6.3%, and ROE is -2.7%, with $57.6M of FY2026 interest expense absorbing much of the operating improvement [1][3][4]. Roughly 3 points of Q1 core growth came from prior-year distributor inventory adjustments and order timing, so underlying growth is closer to 5% [1]. Tangible book value is negative after the 3M merger, R&D intensity is only 2.1% of revenue, and the executive team is newly assembled, leaving execution risk on the FY2031 targets [3][4].
key_catalysts: Raised FY2027 guidance of $885-890M revenue and $181-183M adjusted EBITDA; continued margin expansion toward 20%+ would support a return to GAAP profitability [1]
Execution on the FY2031 targets laid out at the October 2026 Investor Day, including the first organic innovation pipeline under Nassif [2]
Debt paydown reducing the $57.6M annual interest burden, which would flow directly to GAAP EPS [3]
key_risks: Roughly 3 points of Q1 FY2027 core growth were timing-related (distributor inventory and order timing), so growth could decelerate in coming quarters [1]
Persistent GAAP losses (TTM profit margin -6.3%, ROE -2.7%) and negative tangible book value after the 3M merger and $1.09B FY2025 write-down [3][4]
Low R&D intensity (2.1% of revenue) leaves Neogen vulnerable to molecular and rapid-testing platforms from better-funded diagnostics competitors [3]
